findings.correction: Name 98dci4-gpu-0002, job 1339485, two P100 cards and the 224-1803 s per-slice range in lines 42, 45 and 48; identify the 1352.8 s H200 probe as a single-row probe from 98dci4-gpu-0003 that contributed no slice.
findings.text: blocking: the converged section says the job 'ran on one H200 and then on the card the window allowed' and gives the rate as '1352.8 s for 49 passes on one H200' (line 48) with '5.7 h' in the card-time column (line 45), but the landed rows show all 33 converged slices were written by job 1339485 on 98dci4-gpu-0002 (titan, P100) over two cards (the driver's own drift-conv.log line 3 says 'host 98dci4-gpu-0002 job 1339485 converged on 2 cards'), with walls 224.1-1803.1 s summing to 20875.8 s = 5.80 card-hours, while the 1352.8 s fit is a separate one-row probe from job 1339183 on 98dci4-gpu-0003 (H200, one card, slice 0 only, drift-gpu.log line 3) that contributed no slice to the arm. Reporting a titan card-time and rate as an H200 figure is exactly what nova's compute guidance forbids ('a titan number must never carry a throughput or latency headline attributed to the H200'), and it misstates the arm's cost as one H200 rate rather than two P100 cards. The correction is to name the node, the two cards and the 224-1803 s range, and to keep the 1352.8 s H200 probe identified as a probe that contributed no slice.

findings.correction: Move the one-row H200 probe out of the declared arm stem (e.g. nova-white-200-0.0100-probe.jsonl) so grouped() no longer merges it into the 33-slice arm; confirm the arm reduces to 33 rows with one slice 0.
findings.text: blocking: grouped() merges every file matching the declared arm glob under one stem, and the reviewed run left its one-row H200 probe at <cache>/drift-control-20261123/nova-white-200-0.0100.jsonl — the declared nova white stem — beside the 33 converged slices in nova-white-200-0.0100-shard{0,1}.jsonl. The landed reduction therefore reads the arm as 34 rows with slice 0 present twice (49 passes at 1352.8 s from the H200 probe and again at 1667.2 s from the titan refit), and the duplicate inflates the very statistic the study exists to measure: measured with the reviewed head's own analyse.py, the converged arm's axis lag-one is 0.1884 as merged against 0.0903 with slice 0 counted once, flux 0.3328 against 0.2181 and q95 0.3763 against 0.2511. The probe row belongs outside the arm stem (its own name), so it is either stated as the separate probe it is or left out, never merged into the arm.

non-blocking: html_rows emits a fourteen-column body for the two declared arms only (code, sequence, slices, axis_rms, axis_mean_50, flux_rms, flux_mean_50, q95_rms, q95_mean_50 and the five lag-one columns) while the fragment's control table is eleven columns carrying a row-set column, both nova arms and a per-row control verdict, so the emitter cannot reproduce the table the record publishes. Nothing reconciles the new fragment either: test_fragment_tables.py binds only drifting-sensor-probe-rows.html, so a future regeneration cannot reproduce the published table and a drift between the reduction and the record goes uncaught.

non-blocking: the overlay caption says only 'Both null sets are drawn'; the figure rules require that when a solved field is drawn beside the reference one the caption says which marker style belongs to which field, so a reader cannot tell the nova, imas-efit and generating-state null markers apart in the central overlapping markers, and no legend entry names them.

non-blocking: _drawn_tick_labels changes the artifact check that scripts/iron_limb_production/figure.py, scripts/iron_graded_refinement/figure.py, scripts/west_iron_save/figure.py (and other iron_*/magnetisation figure scripts) call through save_checked, and no test exercises it, so a regression in the tick filter silently stops the clipping and overlap check for every one of those figures. The logic is defensible (it filters on the tick's current location against the view limits rather than on the tick's visibility attribute), but it is shared machinery with no guard. No test guards iteration.fit_sequence's resume/refit rule or panel.nova_stem/nova_slice/filter_slice either.

justifications.durability: tests/test_reduction_guards.py:196 drives study.run_nova's own loop and reduces the recorded plasma current (mean lag-one over ten seeds above a literal 0.53), and the negative control at line 214 reinstates the white Gaussian and requires the same reduction inside 0.15, so the landed fix regresses the suite if removed; iteration.py's resume rule, panel.nova_stem/nova_slice and edge_sheet/figure.py's tick filter have no test, and no test pins the one-arm-stem rule that the probe-row collision broke.
justifications.evidence: The gate (analyse.thresholds, check.py) asserts the done-when's lag-one clauses and its result is recorded (CHECK-FAILED nova 1 of 26, reproduced from nova-drift-200-0.0100-shard*.jsonl 0.342/0.626/0.613); I independently recomputed the row-matched block from the arm files with the landed reduction and got 0.481/0.594/0.613; and I recomputed the converged arm from its shard files (33 slices, 26 converged, 7 at the 96-pass cap, 20875.8 s = 5.80 h). Two measured defects cost this score: the 5.7 h and 1352.8 s figures are a titan-to-H200 misattribution (the 33 slices are job 1339485 on 98dci4-gpu-0002, 5.80 card-hours over two P100 cards), and the one-row H200 probe sits at the declared arm stem, so the landed grouped() reduces the arm to 34 rows with slice 0 duplicated and axis lag-one 0.1884 instead of 0.0903.
justifications.fit: The added helpers follow the module idiom (%-formatting, spelled-out docstrings, no classes) and introduce no forbidden name or plan label; the earlier misspelt 'carrries' is corrected at panel.py:110 and the captions match the rendered figures.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The repair is real: reverting study.run_nova's draw to the white Gaussian reproduces the defect (recorded lag-one inside 0.15 in test_run_nova_guard_catches_a_white_current_draw), yet nova's axis mean still reads 0.342/0.481 against the 0.5 floor (docs/evidence/fragments/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/drift-control-and-converged-nova.html:34) and the converged arm covers 33 of 400 slices, so the goal's passing control and converged 200-slice arm are not delivered.
justifications.reuse: study.current_draw wraps the existing noise_columns owner and panel.py reuses analyse.declared_stem, but figures.py:50 and analyse.py:411 re-spell the arm-stem format rather than calling declared_stem, adding two more copies of a naming rule the module already owns.
justifications.scope_discipline: Every path in e28db604e..1acf2fd5b lies inside the declared write paths, and the diff adds nothing the goal does not imply (scripts/edge_sheet/figure.py is declared and its change is the figure check the new figures needed). The two blocking findings are data and content corrections within the declared paths, not scope excess.
